content: New figures from Tussell reveal that public bodies spent £3.4bn on private consultants in the last year, a 62% increase compared to 2019-20. This indicates that spending levels have remained high despite the end of the pandemic. The new Labour government has pledged to cut this expenditure by half during its term, though recent data shows significant contracts, such as a £223m deal with KPMG, were awarded shortly before and after the political transition. Critics, including Labour peer Prem Sikka, argue that the reliance on external advisors is a detrimental trend, claiming these firms offer little value and fail to grasp the complexities of government organizations.
